title: Ukiyo-e
look: A Japanese woodblock print: flat pigments fading in bokashi gradients, a fine key line, washi paper, a curling wave.

doc.essence: An Edo-period colour print: a hair-thin black key block, a handful of mineral and plant pigments, each one wiped into a soft gradient on the block, on fibrous paper with a stylised wave behind.
doc.notIt: Not woodblock (no wood grain, no muted brown inks: indigo, vermilion and ochre fading in bokashi), not ink-wash (colour, a crisp key line, a composed stage), not flat (gradients and paper).
doc.shapes: A fine, even key line. Slightly softer corners and limbs that thin towards their ends, the way a carver's line tapers.
doc.colour: Every area snaps to the nearest of six pigments (indigo, vermilion, ochre, sage, pale pink, paper) and fades from full strength at the top to half strength at the bottom.
doc.eyes: Small sumi-ink eyes with thin brows and a small mouth: a quiet face.
pitfalls: Two roles snapping to the same pigment merge: the key line keeps them apart.
The wave must stay behind the feet, never over the face.
